title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Statute of Limitations in the Trial of Civil Cases

articles.content_en: Article 2: Where a party does not raise a limitation of action defense, the People's Court shall not explain the issue of limitation of action.

Article 3: Where a party fails to raise a limitation of action defense during the first instance trial but raises it during the second instance trial, the People's Court shall not support it, except where the party is able to prove on the basis of new evidence that the claim of the other party has exceeded the limitation period.
Where a party fails to raise a limitation of action defense in accordance with the preceding paragraph, and applies for retrial or raises a retrial defense on the ground that the limitation period has expired, the People's Court shall not support it.

Article 4: Where a contract does not stipulate a time limit for performance, if the time limit for performance can be determined in accordance with Articles 510 and 511 of the Civil Code, the limitation period shall be calculated from the date on which the time limit for performance expires; if the time limit for performance cannot be determined, the limitation period shall be calculated from the date on which the grace period for the creditor to demand the debtor to perform the obligation expires, except that where the debtor explicitly indicates at the time when the creditor first asserts its right against the debtor that it will not perform the obligation, the limitation period shall be calculated from the date on which the debtor explicitly indicates that it will not perform the obligation.

Article 5: Where a party enjoying the right to revocation requests revocation of a contract, the provisions of the Civil Code on the exclusion period shall apply. Where the other party raises a limitation of action defense against the claim for revocation of a contract, the People's Court shall not support it.
Where a contract is revoked, the limitation period for the claim for return of property and compensation for losses shall be calculated from the date on which the contract is revoked.

Article 6: The limitation period for the claim for return of unjust enrichment shall be calculated from the date on which one party knows or should know the facts of unjust enrichment and the other party.

Article 7: The limitation period for the claim of the administrator for payment of necessary management expenses and compensation for losses arising from an act of management without mandate shall be calculated from the date on which the act of management without mandate ends and the administrator knows or should know the principal.
The limitation period for the claim of the principal for compensation for losses arising from an improper act of management without mandate shall be calculated from the date on which the principal knows or should know the administrator and the facts of damage.

Article 9: Where a right holder asserts rights over part of the same claim, the effect of interruption of limitation of action shall extend to the remaining claim, except where the right holder explicitly indicates that it waives the remaining claim.

Article 10: Where one party submits a statement of prosecution to the People's Court or files a prosecution orally, the limitation of action shall be interrupted from the date on which the statement of prosecution is submitted or the oral prosecution is made.

Article 12: Where a right holder submits a request to the People's Mediation Committee and other state organs, public institutions, social organizations and other social organizations that have the authority according to law to resolve relevant civil disputes, to protect the corresponding civil rights, the limitation of action shall be interrupted from the date on which the request is submitted.

Article 13: Where a right holder reports a case to or lodges a complaint with a public security organ, a People's Procuratorate, or a People's Court, requesting protection of its civil rights, the limitation of action shall be interrupted from the date on which the report or complaint is lodged.
Where the aforementioned organ decides not to file the case, withdraws the case, or decides not to prosecute, the limitation period shall be recomputed from the date on which the right holder knows or should know of the decision not to file the case, withdrawal of the case, or decision not to prosecute; where the criminal case enters the trial stage, the limitation period shall be recomputed from the date on which the criminal judgment document takes effect.

Article 14: Where the obligor makes commitments or performs acts such as performing in installments, partial performance, providing security, requesting extension of performance, or formulating a debt repayment plan, it shall be determined that the "obligor agrees to perform the obligation" as provided in Article 195 of the Civil Code has occurred.

Article 15: Where a cause of interruption of limitation of action occurs to one of the joint creditors, it shall be determined that the effect of interruption of limitation of action also occurs to the other joint creditors.
Where a cause of interruption of limitation of action occurs to one of the joint debtors, it shall be determined that the effect of interruption of limitation of action also occurs to the other joint debtors.
Article 16: Where a creditor initiates a subrogation action, it shall be determined that the effect of interruption of limitation of action occurs to both the creditor's claim and the debtor's claim.

Article 17: Where a claim is assigned, it shall be determined that the limitation of action is interrupted from the date on which the notice of assignment of the claim reaches the debtor.
Under the circumstance of assumption of debt, if it constitutes an acknowledgment of the debt by the original debtor, it shall be determined that the limitation of action is interrupted from the date on which the expression of intention to assume the debt reaches the creditor.

Article 18: Where the limitation period for the principal debt has expired, the surety enjoys the right of limitation of action defense of the principal debtor.
Where the surety fails to assert the aforementioned limitation of action defense and, after bearing the suretyship liability, exercises the right of recourse against the principal debtor, the People's Court shall not support it, except where the principal debtor agrees to make payment.

Article 19: Where, after the limitation period expires, one party makes an expression of intention to agree to perform the obligation to the other party or voluntarily performs the obligation, and then raises a defense on the ground that the limitation period has expired, the People's Court shall not support it.
Where the parties conclude a new agreement on the original debt, and the creditor claims that the obligor has waived the limitation of action defense, the People's Court shall support it.
Where, after the limitation period has expired, the lender issues a notice of demand for payment of an overdue loan to the borrower, and the debtor signs or seals on the notice, if it can be determined that the borrower agrees to perform the obligation that has already expired by limitation, the People's Court shall support the lender's claim that the borrower has waived the limitation of action defense.

Article 20: After these Provisions come into force, where a case is still in the first instance or second instance stage, these Provisions shall apply; where a case has already been finally adjudicated before these Provisions come into force, these Provisions shall not apply when the People's Court conducts a retrial.

Article 21: Where the relevant judicial interpretations made by this Court before these Provisions come into force conflict with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
